parq.intro: This short screening helps us determine your readiness for physical activity.
parq.q1: 1. Has your doctor ever said that you have a heart condition and that you should only do physical activity recommended by a doctor?
parq.q2: 2. Do you feel pain in your chest when you do physical activity?
parq.q3: 3. In the past month, have you had chest pain when you were not doing physical activity?
parq.q4: 4. Do you lose your balance because of dizziness or do you ever lose consciousness?
parq.q5: 5. Do you have a bone or joint problem (for example, back, knee, or hip) that could be made worse by a change in your physical activity?
parq.q6: 6. Is your doctor currently prescribing drugs (for example, water pills) for your blood pressure or heart condition?
parq.q7: 7. Do you know of any other reason why you should not do physical activity?
parq.congratsSubtitle: You are ready to safely start your personalized exercise plan in OncoSmart.
parq.consultSubtitle: For your safety, please consult your doctor before starting this exercise plan

daySession.subtitle: Gentle moves to restore strength and support healing
daySession.pulseSubtitle: Make sure your heart rate stays below {{bpm}} (bpm) during exercise session
daySession.manualTitle: Count Your Pulse at the Wrist
daySession.manualBody: Place two fingers on the side of your wrist, just below your thumb. Count how many beats you feel in 1 minute, and note that number as your pulse rate (bpm).
daySession.oximeter1Body: A quick guide to measuring your oxygen levels.
daySession.oximeter2Body: Gently open the pulse oximeter before placing your finger.
daySession.oximeter3Body: Slide your fingertip into the device.
daySession.oximeter4Body: Make sure your finger is positioned comfortably.
daySession.oximeter5Body: Keep still while the device measures your levels.
daySession.oximeter6Body: The circled number next to the heart is your pulse.
daySession.oximeter7Body: You can now check your oxygen levels whenever needed.
daySession.allowedBpm: Allowed heart rate for your age: up to {{bpm}} bpm
daySession.bpmTooHigh: Your heart rate exceeds the allowed limit for your age.
daySession.bpmInvalid: Enter a valid heart rate between 1 and 250 bpm.
daySession.consultDoctor: Please consult your doctor before exercising.
daySession.endBpmTitle: How is your heart rate now?
daySession.endBpmSubtitle: Enter your current heart rate (bpm) after finishing the session.

diaphragmatic-breathing.title: Diaphragmatic Breathing
diaphragmatic-breathing.description: Improves lung expansion and helps you breathe better. Sit upright on a chair. Place one hand on your chest and the other on your abdomen. Breathe in slowly through your nose, feel your abdomen rise, and breathe out gently through your mouth.

ankle-pumps.title: Ankle Pumps
ankle-pumps.description: Improves blood circulation and prevents stiffness in the legs. Sit upright on the bed with your legs straight. Slowly move your feet up and down.

thoracic-expansion.title: Thoracic Expansion Exercise
thoracic-expansion.description: Improves chest expansion and lung capacity. Take a deep breath while expanding your chest. Hold for a few seconds and slowly breathe out.

arm-circles.title: Arm Circles
arm-circles.description: Improves shoulder mobility and circulation. Lift your arms and slowly rotate them in circular motion.

spot-marching.title: Spot Marching
spot-marching.description: Improves circulation and endurance. Stand straight and march in place by lifting knees alternately.

shoulder-shrugging.title: Shoulder Shrugging
shoulder-shrugging.description: Relieves shoulder tension and improves mobility. Lift both shoulders towards your ears and slowly relax.

biceps-curls.title: Biceps Curls
biceps-curls.description: Strengthens arm muscles. Bend your elbows and bring your hands toward your shoulders, then slowly lower.

wall-pushup.title: Wall Push-up
wall-pushup.description: Improves upper-body strength. Stand facing the wall with your hands at shoulder height. Slowly bend your elbows and lean toward the wall. Then gently push back to the starting position.

calf-raise.title: Calf Raises
calf-raise.description: Strengthens the lower leg muscles and improves balance. Stand upright with your hands on the wall for support. Slowly lift your heels off the floor. Then slowly lower your heels back down.

sit-to-stand.title: Sit-to-Stand
sit-to-stand.description: Strengthens lower body muscles and improves balance. Start in a sitting position on a chair, slowly stand up, then sit down again in a controlled manner.

straight-leg-raise-right.title: Straight Leg Raise (Right)
straight-leg-raise-right.description: Strengthens the thigh muscles and improves leg strength. Lie comfortably on your back on the bed. Keep your right knee straight and slowly lift your right leg as far as comfortable. Then slowly lower your leg back down.

straight-leg-raise-left.title: Straight Leg Raise (Left)
straight-leg-raise-left.description: Strengthens the thigh muscles and improves leg strength. Lie comfortably on your back on the bed. Keep your left knee straight and slowly lift your left leg as far as comfortable. Then slowly lower your leg back down.

knee-to-chest-right.title: Knee to Chest (Right)
knee-to-chest-right.description: Improves hip mobility and reduces stiffness. Lie on your back with the left leg straight. Using your hands, bring your right knee toward your chest, then slowly return to the starting position.

knee-to-chest-left.title: Knee to Chest (Left)
knee-to-chest-left.description: Improves hip mobility and reduces stiffness. Lie on your back with the right leg straight. Using your hands, bring your left knee toward your chest, then slowly return to the starting position.

static-quadriceps-right.title: Static Quadriceps (Right)
static-quadriceps-right.description: Strengthens thigh muscles and improves knee control. Sit with your legs stretched forward. Slowly press your right knee toward the floor, hold briefly, then relax.

static-quadriceps-left.title: Static Quadriceps (Left)
static-quadriceps-left.description: Strengthens thigh muscles and improves knee control. Sit with your legs stretched forward. Slowly press your left knee toward the floor, hold briefly, then relax.

hamstring-stretch.title: Hamstring Stretch
hamstring-stretch.description: Improves flexibility of the back of the thigh. Sit on the bed with your legs straight. Slowly lean forward and reach toward your toes. Feel a gentle stretch behind your thighs.

quadriceps-stretch-right.title: Quadriceps Stretch (Right)
quadriceps-stretch-right.description: Improves flexibility of the front thigh muscles. Stand upright and hold the chair for support. Bend your right knee as far as comfortable and gently pull your foot toward your buttock to stretch the front of your thigh.

quadriceps-stretch-left.title: Quadriceps Stretch (Left)
quadriceps-stretch-left.description: Improves flexibility of the front thigh muscles. Stand upright and hold the chair for support. Bend your left knee as far as comfortable and gently pull your foot toward your buttock to stretch the front of your thigh.

calf-stretch-right.title: Calf Stretch (Right)
calf-stretch-right.description: Helps stretch the muscles at the back of the lower leg. Stand upright with your hands on the wall at shoulder height. Keep your right leg straight behind you with your heel on the floor. Gently lean forward until you feel a stretch in the back of your lower leg.

calf-stretch-left.title: Calf Stretch (Left)
calf-stretch-left.description: Helps stretch the muscles at the back of the lower leg. Stand upright with your hands on the wall at shoulder height. Keep your left leg straight behind you with your heel on the floor. Gently lean forward until you feel a stretch in the back of your lower leg.

chest-stretch.title: Pectoralis Stretch
chest-stretch.description: Improves flexibility of the chest muscles. Stand in a doorframe with your hands at shoulder height. Gently lean forward until you feel a stretch across the front of your chest.

triceps-stretch-right.title: Triceps Stretch (Right)
triceps-stretch-right.description: Helps stretch the muscles at the back of the upper arm. Place your right arm behind your head and gently pull the right elbow with your left hand. Feel a stretch at the back of your right upper arm.

triceps-stretch-left.title: Triceps Stretch (Left)
triceps-stretch-left.description: Helps stretch the muscles at the back of the upper arm. Place your left arm behind your head and gently pull the left elbow with your right hand. Feel a stretch at the back of your left upper arm.

neck-stretch-right.title: Neck Stretch (Right)
neck-stretch-right.description: Helps improve neck movement. Stand upright with your shoulders relaxed. Slowly tilt your head towards your left shoulder. Gently apply pressure with your left hand. You should feel a stretch along the right side of your neck.

neck-stretch-left.title: Neck Stretch (Left)
neck-stretch-left.description: Helps improve neck movement. Stand upright with your shoulders relaxed. Slowly tilt your head towards your right shoulder. Gently apply pressure with your right hand. You should feel a stretch along the left side of your neck.
